focus_title: A people marked by migration and resilience
focus_text1: The Volga Germans constitute one of the most significant migrant communities in modern history. Their origin dates back to the 18th century, when thousands of families were invited to settle on the banks of the Volga River, in the then Russian Empire. There they developed prosperous agricultural colonies, preserving for generations their language, traditions and institutions.
focus_text2: However, social, political and economic crises drove new migratory waves to different countries of the Americas, including Argentina, Brazil, the United States, Canada and other destinations where they continued building communities that still preserve part of their cultural identity. This project seeks to contribute to the knowledge of that history through the study of documentary sources, demographic data, cartography, genealogy and statistical analysis, with the purpose of preserving historical heritage, strengthening collective memory and generating scientific knowledge about the territorial and social evolution of these communities.
